selection.rationale: Objective ttft_ms is measured at the source's explicit first-token boundary (adapter run(): the Qwen3ForCausalLM prefill forward on the frozen [1,256] int64 input_ids with use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1, the logits[:,-1] select, argmax, and torch.cuda.synchronize), so the only coherent editable boundary that can move the metric is that whole prefill region; decode (~23294 observed calls) is outside the objective and stays untouched. Measured facts from current discovery on revision 4fd93590c6d: the region's single module call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f) spans 3675 descendant prefill calls plus the two boundary consumers, contributing only 20.86 ms of nested diagnostic CUDA (16.67 ms across the 253 prefill aten::linear calls, 0.82 ms across the 36 SDPA calls, the rest pointwise/embedding/rotary), while the current accepted version's fresh-worker ttft is 65.73/67.72 ms (median 66.72 ms, paired noise bounds 1.80/1.83 ms) - i.e. roughly 46 ms of TTFT is host-side per-call dispatch across the wrapped prefill path (the inherited effective pointwise bundle trial-resample-3896551a-param-102dba91 plus framework routing), not GPU work. The previous trial on exactly this region passed numerics and timing only by falling back: its build-time BITWISE gate torch.equal(static_out.logits, warm.logits) (previous candidate.py lines 226-229) returned False, so every new-call route was prefill_guard_parent, the graph never replayed, and effective coexistence was judged unsatisfied; that gate defect, not the boundary and not the mechanism, is the concrete failure to repair. Per-kernel or per-family replacement inside the region is the wrong boundary for this objective: total prefill GEMM CUDA is 16.67 ms and the earlier joint GEMM trial regressed ttft to 89.83 ms through wrapper overhead when its sites fell back, while a genuinely executing whole-region replay removes essentially the entire ~46 ms host component at once. Composition is structural: the inherited bundle's prefill-site fused kernels are ordinary kernels launched by the parent path and are captured inside the graph, and its decode sites (running eagerly 31 times per site) are untouched; my write set is exactly the one region call, disjoint from the inherited bundle's call writes. affected_calls is re-derived from current discovery: the region's module call, all 3675 observed prefill-phase calls in its subtree (embedding, rotary, all decoder-layer module and aten calls including the pointwise calls owned by the installed bundle, all 253 linears, 36 SDPA calls), and the boundary consumers e8e33b0c65e0a9187702157b (aten::select.int on logits) and f5db82bcffb946a3610cd8fe (prefill aten::argmax); discovery profiler instrumentation calls are excluded.
selection.hypothesis: Repair-and-retest of the whole-prefill CUDA-graph execution policy at the same region boundary, as a hypothesis for paired measurement. Diagnosis to test first on the leased worker: the previous guard compared one graph replay against one eager warm run BITWISE, which conflates three untested causes - (a) eager prefill may not be bitwise run-to-run deterministic on this stack (cuBLAS/SDPA algorithm or accumulation variation between runs), (b) graph-private-pool allocations change pointer alignment versus regular allocator blocks, switching cuBLAS/SDPA kernel selection and bf16 accumulation order (the same class of difference that broke trial-9cc583939d under a bit-exactness gate but which sits far inside this task's frozen atol=rtol=0.02 logits tolerance), or (c) the capture_error_mode='thread_local' fallback recorded an inconsistent capture. The repair keeps the mechanism (build-time untimed capture of the current parent forward on a side stream after warmup, per-run static input copy, single graph replay, logits clone and fresh deep-copied DynamicCache handed to the untouched decode loop, all on the calling stream inside the declared boundary with no added synchronization and no precomputed or cached outputs) but gates activation on the frozen request's actual quality contract instead of bitwise equality: logits within atol=rtol=0.02, exact equality of the greedy argmax token, and per-layer KV within tolerance against a fresh eager parent run, preceded by an eager-vs-eager bitwise comparison to distinguish (a) from (b), with the capture attempted under the default global error mode and only well-justified fallback; distinct actual route labels must distinguish active replay from every fallback, and a guard-failure category must be retained so effective coexistence is verifiable rather than assumed - the external evaluator stays authoritative and is not relaxed. If the gate passes, replay re-executes the identical 1420-kernel prefill stream while removing the ~46 ms host dispatch component, so ttft should fall from ~66.7 ms toward the ~21 ms GPU-bound floor (a gain far above both ~1.8 ms noise bounds) with decode_ms unchanged; if eager nondeterminism or a real replay mismatch makes even the tolerance contract unsafe (argmax near-tie flip), the policy must remain disabled and be reported as an honest negative result rather than shipping a silently-falling-back wrapper.

proposal.rationale: inputs/previous-feedback.txt changes this attempt in two concrete ways. First, the prior trial trial-023e79293c was accepted by numerical/timing rules but every invocation routed to the parent: its build-time BITWISE gate torch.equal(static_out.logits, warm.logits) (candidate lines 226-229, confirmed by observed_guard and the candidate_diagnostics False-return at _try_build_graph) rejected an otherwise successful capture+replay, conflating eager run-to-run nondeterminism and graph-private-pool cuBLAS/SDPA kernel-selection differences with real invalidity, so effective coexistence was judged unsatisfied. Second, verified framework mechanics (kernel_optimizer/project/{evaluation,binding,discovery}.py under /root/autodl-tmp/dev/opop-v6-freezes/6d71a3c45c61): bundles install before operation(); inherited functional replacements engage only inside the BindingSession ReplacementMode that operation() enters around adapter.run, and inherited phase-guarded module replacements engage only under the matching discovery phase - so the prior BUILD-time capture necessarily recorded the raw eager stream and the selection's assumption that the graph contains the inherited kernels was unproven and false in general. Repair: this candidate replaces exactly the same single site 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a (Qwen3ForCausalLM prefill module call, input_ids=[1,256] int64, use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1) with a whole-prefill CUDA Graph replay policy whose initialization is LAZY: build() performs no GPU work and returns one callable; the first legitimate invocation runs inside adapter.run's prefill phase with the inherited dispatch modes entered, so its warmup forwards and the capture execute the true current parent implementation and the captured kernel stream preserves the inherited bundle's fused pointwise kernels (functional sites) and module replacements under every later replay. Activation is gated on the frozen request quality contract, never on bitwise equality: logits allclose atol=rtol=0.02, exact greedy argmax of the first token, per-layer KV within the same tolerance against a fresh eager parent run, and an end-to-end exact greedy token equality over the full 32-token decode (two decode loops run under discovery phase 'decode' from materialized eager-KV and replay-KV caches); an eager-vs-eager bitwise probe is recorded for diagnosis only. Capture is attempted under the default global error mode with a single thread_local retry on capture exception; an inconsistent capture is still caught by the full downstream verification. Any failure permanently disables the policy with retained categories and distinct route labels (prefill_graph_replay; prefill_init_setup_parent, prefill_init_capture_parent, prefill_init_verify_parent; prefill_signature_parent; prefill_replay_error_parent; prefill_clone_failed_parent). Every invocation then executes the complete current-input workload: copy input_ids into the 2 KiB static buffer, one graph replay re-running the captured prefill kernel stream, clone of the [1,1,151936] bf16 logits, materialization of a fresh ~36.9 MiB KV cache via torch.cat out of the graph private pool (DynamicCache.update is pure cat on transformers 5.16.1, verified on the worker Python /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python), all on the calling stream inside the declared ttft boundary with no added run-time synchronization; decode is untouched. Coexistence accounting: the inherited trial-resample-3896551a-param-102dba91 bundle's 577 prefill-phase sites inside this region (432 functional + 145 module) dispatch eagerly during the initialization invocation - which is the first tracked quality run, providing their coverage counts - and their fused kernels are captured into and re-executed by every replay; its 577 decode-phase sites keep executing eagerly every run (31 steps per run); both installed implementations therefore contribute computation, and this bundle explicitly replaces the ineffective trial-023e79293c-param-3d3884d7 write on the same site while requiring the inherited pointwise bundle to stay installed. The 3677 inner prefill-region calls listed in eliminated_calls no longer dispatch through Python during steady replay invocations; their work is preserved as native kernels inside the graph, their consumers receive value-equivalent outputs (gated against a fresh eager run), and the framework can recapture the plan. Expected effect, as a hypothesis for paired measurement: the objective is host-dispatch bound - current discovery measures the selected call at 20855 us diagnostic CUDA over 1420 kernels (target-resources.json) while accepted ttft medians ~65.7-67.7 ms with paired noise bounds ~1.8 ms - so replay should move ttft toward the GPU-bound floor plus bounded copy/clone host overhead; a disabled-path outcome (any gate failure) is a valid negative result that leaves the eager parent, and the inherited bundle, fully in charge. No fixture outputs are precomputed or cached: the graph recomputes everything from the caller's current input buffer each run.
proposal.setup_work: build(context) performs no GPU work and returns {900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a: callable}. All setup is lazy inside the first legitimate invocation of that callable, which lands in the untimed first quality-mode run (evaluation.py runs quality invokes before any measured sample; profile actions run warmup invokes before profiling). Setup stages, all through the current parent reference with the inherited dispatch modes entered and phase=prefill: (1) three eager warmup prefill forwards on a side stream (allocator, cuBLAS and inherited-kernel warmup); (2) one CUDA graph capture under the default global error mode (single thread_local retry on capture exception only); (3) one replay plus verification gates; (4) two 31-step verification decode loops under discovery phase 'decode'; (5) cache materialization and output-construction probes. Memory, reported explicitly: retained after setup are the 2 KiB static input buffer and the CUDA graph private pool holding the captured region's intermediates, KV and logits workspace - reserved memory that persists for the session rather than being freed per run; per-run regular-pool allocations are the logits clone (~0.29 MiB for [1,1,151936] bf16) and the materialized KV cache (36 layers x 2 tensors of [1,8,256,128] bf16 = 36 MiB, plus one transient cat copy per tensor). Warm-run peak_allocated counters may fall when prefill intermediates move into the retained graph pool while reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peaks (which include the capture-time transient and subsequent invocations) increase; that is an accounting redistribution between pools, not a physical-memory saving, and no counter here measures non-PyTorch driver allocation.
quality_risks: Graph replay is not guaranteed bitwise-equal to eager execution: graph-private-pool allocations can change cuBLAS/SDPA kernel selection and bf16 accumulation order. Mitigated by gating activation on the frozen contract (logits atol=rtol=0.02, exact first greedy token, per-layer KV within tolerance, and exact equality of the full 32-token greedy sequence on the actual frozen input); any violation permanently disables replay (prefill_init_verify_parent) and the region runs the eager parent.

Exact greedy tokens are checked end-to-end at initialization against the same-process eager parent; eager greedy generation is deterministic for this frozen workload (the source itself asserts exact regeneration), so a passed gate carries to validation runs, but an argmax near-tie between replay and eager numerics would disable the path rather than risk a token mismatch.

Capture under the entered dispatch mode could fail if any engaged inherited kernel is capture-unsafe; the failure is caught (setup/capture categories retained), thread_local is retried once and any inconsistent capture is still caught by verification; on total failure the eager parent path is unchanged, bounding the outcome at the currently accepted behavior.

Decode consumes a freshly materialized regular-allocator cache each run (torch.cat copies out of the graph pool; verified pure-cat semantics on transformers 5.16.1), so no aliasing between decode state and graph-pool memory exists across runs.

Run-time overhead inside the ttft boundary is bounded: one 2 KiB copy, one graph launch, one logits clone and ~72 small cat launches for cache materialization; this cannot regress beyond the eager baseline unless replay is disabled, in which case the parent path is taken.

Coverage: during steady replay invocations the region's inner dispatch events disappear (listed in eliminated_calls); the inherited prefill sites still dispatch and count during the initialization invocation (first tracked quality run), and inherited decode sites count on every run, so installed bundle coverage does not depend on fabricated counts.
Retained graph-pool memory increases framework reserved bytes and lifecycle peaks; documented in setup_work, not claimed as a saving.
